_comment: Editor UI metadata for the Loss Recovery LEG — labels, groups, plain-English descriptions and the 'essentials' (core) flag. Read by the command-center scanner and overlaid onto the schema built from RecoveryLabConfig. UI ONLY: it never touches a trade decision. NO PINE TWIN EXISTS for this package, so — unlike every strategy meta here — there is no label/tooltip sync rule and no parity gate to re-run; a label may be written for the lab alone. COPY STYLE (matching mpc_sos_fade.meta.json): every desc is SHORT and PLAIN — what the setting does, what each choice means, and the one fact that changes the decision. No measurement dumps, no trade counts, no R figures, no dates. The evidence behind a default lives in this package's CLAUDE.md. THIS RULE CANNOT RUN ALONE: the package declares requires_source, so it never appears in a strategy picker — it is added by ticking it under a parent in the stack builder, and it reads that parent's losses.
edge: It does not find its own trades. Every time the strategy it is attached to takes a loss, this waits for the market to turn back the other way and takes a smaller trade in that direction, to win the loss back. It aims for about one unit of profit and then protects it.

steps.label: 01 · Wait
steps.title: The parent takes a loss
steps.detail: Nothing happens until the strategy this is attached to closes a real loss. A scratch does not count.

steps.label: 02 · Turn
steps.title: Structure breaks back the other way
steps.detail: It waits for the market to break structure against the direction that just lost. That break is the signal.

steps.label: 03 · Enter
steps.title: A smaller trade, the other way
steps.detail: It enters at the next bar's open, at a fraction of a normal trade's risk. The stop goes at the far end of the move that broke structure.

steps.label: 04 · Protect
steps.title: Lock the recovery in
steps.detail: Once the trade has travelled far enough to have paid the loss back, the stop moves up to bank it. After that it trails behind structure.

params.name: rec_risk_frac
params.label: Size next to a normal trade
params.desc: How big a recovery trade is compared with one of the parent strategy's. 0.25 means a quarter of the usual risk. It follows the parent, so raising the parent's risk raises this too.
guide: Smaller recoveries, and less room taken off the parent
Bigger recoveries, and a bigger drawdown with them

params.name: rec_both_dirs
params.label: Recover in either direction
params.desc: Whether to take the recovery whichever way it points. Turning this off keeps only the direction that happened to win in the past, which is a decision made after seeing the answer.

params.name: rec_scratch_r
params.label: What counts as a real loss
params.desc: A parent trade that finished this close to breakeven counts as a scratch, not a loss, so it arms nothing. Raise it and fewer trades arm a recovery.

params.name: rec_stop_mode
params.label: Where the stop goes
params.desc: structural = the far end of the move that broke structure, which is the tested rule. loss_entry = the price the losing trade entered at, which is much tighter and was measured to lose money. leg_frac = part of the way back, set below. The three volatility-based placements this rule also has cannot run here, because two strategies sharing one account have no shared volatility reading.

params.name: rec_stop_leg_frac
params.label: ↳ How much of the move to keep
params.desc: 0.5 puts the stop halfway between the entry and the far end. 1.0 is the same as the structural placement. A tighter stop does not risk less — it buys a bigger position for the same money.

params.name: rec_lock_at_r
params.label: Move the stop once it has travelled
params.desc: How far the recovery has to run in your favour before the stop is moved up. 1 is the point where the original loss has been paid back.

params.name: rec_lock_to_r
params.label: ↳ Where the stop goes
params.desc: Where the stop lands once it moves. 1 banks the recovery. 0 is plain breakeven, which stops you losing but does not bank the thing you entered for.

params.name: rec_soft_stop_r
params.label: Give up early once it is against you
params.desc: Close a losing recovery once it is this far against you, instead of waiting for the full stop. 0 leaves the full stop in place. This is the only setting here that makes a losing recovery cost less, because it does not move the distance the trade was sized on.

params.name: rec_trail_swings
params.label: Trail behind structure
params.desc: After the stop has moved up, keep dragging it behind each new confirmed turn. Off leaves it where it was locked.

params.name: rec_invalidate_on_choch
params.label: Close if structure turns against it
params.desc: Close the recovery early if the market breaks structure back against it. Measured and it costs money — the turn usually arrives after the damage is done.

params.name: rec_max_days
params.label: Give up after this many days
params.desc: Close a recovery that has gone nowhere after this long. A backstop — most finish well inside it. It exists because trades left open for months pay a lot of overnight interest.
